item.title: New York lawmakers introduce data center development moratorium
item.description: Data centers may no longer be coming to a town near New Yorkers if a pair of state legislators get their way. State Sen. Liz Krueger and Assembly member Anna Kelles introduced a bill that would create a three-year moratorium on data center development in the state, Wired reported. item.title: Citadel’s Ken Griffin takes stake in 350 Park, readies for demolition
item.description: Citadel’s Ken Griffin decided to take a 60 percent stake in the joint venture that will transform 350 Park Avenue. item.title: Linklaters expands at Vornado’s 1290 Sixth Avenue
item.description: Global law firm Linklaters is bulking up in Midtown. The London-based firm is adding 48,000 square feet at Vornado Realty Trust’s 1290 Sixth Avenue, The Real Deal has learned. Linklaters signed a 10-year lease for a portion of the building’s 11th floor, bringing its total footprint at the tower to more than 150,000 square feet. item.title: Ranco, Gilardians secure $115M loan at Murray Hill project
item.description: Ranco Capital and the Gilardian family are approaching the checkered flag on a luxury rental development in Murray Hill, securing a nine-figure loan to push the development across the finish line. Ranco and the Gilardians landed a $115 million loan to refinance the 22-story project at 162 East 36th Street, the Commercial Observer reported. item.title: One Domino could beat its own Williamsburg condo price record
item.description: Two Trees’ One Domino Square is competing against itself. Just over six months after setting the record for the priciest condo sold in North Brooklyn on a per-square-foot basis, the waterfront development put another penthouse into contract that is on pace to beat that mark. Penthouse 3A is under contract for $7 million, according to a spokesperson for the project. item.title: Jonathan Miller and Douglas Elliman break up data partnership after 32 years
item.description: Appraiser Jonathan Miller’s relationship with Douglas Elliman is coming to a close after 32 years.
